passages.heading: Debt note
passages.text: 19. Borrowings All borrowings are initially recorded at fair value, net of transaction costs. Borrowings are subsequently carried at amortised cost, with the difference between the proceeds, net of transaction costs, and the amount due on redemption being recognised as a charge to the income statement over the period of the relevant borrowing. ​ Lease liabilities The corresponding liability to the lessor is recognised as a lease obligation within short term and long-term borrowings. The carrying amount is subsequently increased to reflect interest on the lease liability and reduced by lease payments made. ​ For calculating the discounted lease liability on leases, the implicit rate in the lease is used. If this is not available, the incremental borrowing rate with a lease-specific adjustment is used. Finance costs are charged to the income statement to produce a constant periodic rate of charge on the remaining balance of the obligations for each accounting period. ​ Variable rents are not part of the lease liability and the right of use asset. These payments are charged to the income statement as incurred. Short term and low-value leases are not capitalised, and lease rentals are also charged to the income statement as incurred. ​

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The Group has identified a broad range of risks relating to its business and the industry in which it operates. These risks are described below and, together with all other information contained in this Annual Report, should be carefully considered in evaluating the Group. The risks and uncertainties described below represent those we consider to be material as at the date of this Annual Report, with material risks being those to which senior management pay particular attention and which could cause the delivery of the Group’s strategy, financial condition, results of operations and/or prospects to differ materially from expectations. However, these risks and uncertainties are not the only ones facing the Group. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects could be materially and adversely affected. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations. Risks relating to the Group’s business and industry The Group operates in a highly competitive market The Group faces substantial and increasing competition in all of its product categories and geographic markets. There are relatively low barriers to entry in certain product categories in many of the markets in which the Group operates (particularly in the VMS category) and accordingly the Group’s businesses compete with companies of all sizes on many different fronts, including cost-effectiveness, product effectiveness and quality, brand recognition and loyalty, technological innovations, consumer convenience, promotional activities, new product introductions and expansion into new markets and channels. The Group expects to continue to see heightened activity from its competitors worldwide, including: (i) increasing and aggressive competition from smaller, high-growth companies which often operate on a regional basis, and may disrupt existing route-to-market models; (ii) increasing competition from multinational corporations moving for the first time into, or expanding or focusing their presence (whether through acquisitions, disposals, demergers or other means) in the global consumer healthcare market; (iii) continuing competition from private label products, which are brands sold exclusively by a particular retailer; and (iv) an increase in the introduction and aggressive marketing of new products in high-demand healthcare areas. Some of the Group’s competitors may conduct more effective advertising and promotion activities than the Group does, introduce competing products more quickly and/or respond more effectively to business and economic conditions and changing consumer preferences, including by launching innovative new products. These risks could also be enhanced by the relatively recent development of generative AI and its rapidly evolving nature, which could enable new or existing competitors who are better able to capitalise on these developments to achieve additional competitive advantages, such as enhanced product targeting or cost-savings on advertising and promotion. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin expanded year over year and now sits well above the consumer staples sector median, reflecting pricing power and cost discipline in the consumer healthcare portfolio. This earnings quality underpins the group's capacity to absorb input-cost and promotional pressure without eroding cash generation.

Free cash flow to debt improved year over year and exceeds the sector median, with capital expenditure modest relative to operating cash flow. The group converts earnings into cash efficiently, leaving headroom for debt reduction or distributions without straining the balance sheet.

key_risks.text: The group operates in a highly competitive market with relatively low barriers to entry, particularly in the VMS category, facing private label, smaller high-growth entrants and multinational expansion. Aggressive promotion and generative AI-enabled competitor targeting could pressure pricing and margins, weakening the cash flow that services debt.

Gross and net leverage sit above the sector median, though both declined year over year as borrowings fell. The indicative intermediate risk profile leaves limited headroom to the next leverage band, so an earnings setback or debt-funded action would tighten the position.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved year over year and remains comfortably above unity, though it sits below the sector median. Operating income covers finance costs several times over, and the debt note confirms borrowings are carried at amortised cost with costs spread over the borrowing period, so refinancing terms will drive future charges.

Operating cash flow to debt improved year over year and exceeds the sector median, while the current ratio sits below both the prior year and the sector median. The group therefore relies on recurring cash generation rather than balance-sheet liquidity to meet near-term obligations.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative intermediate financial risk profile rests on leverage below the next risk-band boundary and cash flow coverage above its threshold, with the Altman zone safe. Deleveraging year over year and superior margins support a stable credit trajectory, though the position is not strong enough to absorb a material earnings shock.

Analyst judgement: free cash flow appears ample relative to capital expenditure, but the bundle does not disclose dividends or buybacks, so the share of cash flow absorbed by shareholder returns is unknown. Until distribution data is available, the durability of deleveraging cannot be fully assessed.

credit_strengths.text: 營業利潤率按年擴大，現時遠高於消費必需品行業中位數，反映消費保健產品組合的定價能力及成本紀律。此盈利質素支撐集團在不侵蝕現金生成的情況下吸收投入成本及促銷壓力的能力。
自由現金流對債務比率按年改善並高於行業中位數，資本開支相對經營現金流溫和。集團高效地將盈利轉化為現金，為減債或分派留有空間而不致令資產負債表受壓。

key_risks.text: 集團經營於競爭激烈的市場，進入壁壘相對較低，尤其在 VMS 類別，面對自有品牌、較小的高增長進入者及跨國擴張。激進促銷及生成式 AI 賦能的競爭對手定向營銷可能對定價及利潤率構成壓力，削弱償付債務的現金流。
總槓桿及淨槓桿高於行業中位數，儘管兩者均按年下降，因借款減少。指示性 intermediate 風險狀況對下一槓桿區間留有有限空間，因此盈利挫折或債務融資行動將收緊該狀況。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年改善並穩居於一以上，儘管低於行業中位數。經營收入覆蓋財務成本數倍，且債務附註確認借款按攤銷成本列賬，成本於借款期內分攤，因此再融資條款將驅動未來費用。
經營現金流對債務比率按年改善並高於行業中位數，而流動比率低於去年及行業中位數。因此集團依賴經常性現金生成而非資產負債表流動性來履行短期義務。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性 intermediate 財務風險狀況基於槓桿低於下一風險區間邊界及現金流覆蓋高於其門檻，Altman 區域為安全。按年去槓桿及優越利潤率支撐穩定的信用軌跡，儘管該狀況不足以吸收重大盈利衝擊。
分析師判斷：自由現金流相對資本開支似乎充裕，但該組合未披露股息或回購，因此股東回報所吸收的現金流份額未知。在分派數據可得之前，去槓桿的持久性無法全面評估。
